          Why Aren’t Arsenal Scoring Any Corners?
        
      
                          
                      Oct 24, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Arsenal broke the Premier League record for goals from corners last season, but seven games into their title defence, they haven’t scored from a single one yet in 2026-27. What’s going wrong for the set-piece specialists?
By now, we all know the story of Arsenal’s first Premier League title in 22 years.

It was a success built not on a fierce, free-flowing attack, but on an exceptional defence, the deepest squad in the division, and an ability to master the fine margins of football better than anyone else.
Nowhere was that more evident than at set-pieces.

Arsenal exploited corners to devastating effect in 2025-26. They broke the record for the number of goals scored from corners in a single Premier League season with 19, and their 26.8% of goals coming from corners was comfortably the highest share of any Premier League champion.

Even with referees paying closer attention to grappling and blocking at corners this season, the expectation was that Arsenal would continue to lean heavily into their set-piece strength. Why wouldn’t they?

But that hasn’t transpired. We’re seven league games into the new campaign, and Arsenal haven’t scored a single goal from a corner. In fact, across all competitions, they haven’t scored from any non-penalty set-piece at all.
At the same stage of last season, they’d already scored six goals from corners in the league alone.
So, what’s going on? Are ‘Set-Piece FC’ suddenly… bad at set-pieces? Or is there another explanation?

Let’s just check the premise. Given we’re only seven games into the season, goals alone don't necessarily tell us the full story as to how effective Arsenal’s corners have been. For a better look under the hood, we can turn to our old friend expected goals (xG).
Last season, Arsenal led the Premier League for total xG generated from corners, with 13.8. That worked out at 0.36 xG per game, at an average of 0.064 xG per corner.

Put another way, when Arsenal took a corner, there was a 6.4% chance that it would result in a goal, the second-best value of any team. Arsenal slightly overperformed in reality, scoring from 8.8% of all their corners – the highest rate of any team.
This season, though, things have changed.
Arsenal are generating just 0.22 xG per game from corners, at an average of 0.047 xG per corner. They've fallen from the second-most dangerous team per corner to the ninth.
A drop from 0.064 to 0.047 might not sound particularly dramatic, but it represents a 26.6% reduction in the average quality of chances they’re generating per corner.

And it’s not just the quality of chances that has declined. Arsenal are also generating fewer shots from corners, down from 2.8 per game last season, the second-highest figure in the league, to 2.1 this season, the ninth highest.

Before we get into trying to work out why, it’s worth saying that Arsenal have still generated 1.55 xG from corners this season. That's the seventh-highest total in the Premier League and suggests they could reasonably have expected to score at least once. In fact, only Liverpool (-2.05) have underperformed their corner xG by a greater margin than Arsenal (-1.55).
So, what’s with the drop-off? Has Arsenal’s approach changed?
In 2025-26, Arsenal crossed the ball into the penalty area from 86.6% of their corners, opting to go short on 13.0% of occasions.
This season, those shares haven’t changed much. They're crossing from 84.9% of corners and playing short from the remaining 15.1%.
